crop: Cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.), open-field slicing type
naming_warning: In Cameroonian French, 'concombre' very often designates the seed cucurbit Cucumeropsis mannii (ngon, Ewondo), grown for dried seeds, not the fresh table cucumber Cucumis sativus (S27, S28). National statistics labelled 'concombre' or FAO 'cucumbers and gherkins' for Cameroon may mix both. Every Cameroon figure below must be read with this caveat.

cycle.establishment: Mostly direct sowing in the field, 2 seeds per hole (Benin, S1), 3 seeds per hill (Ngaoundere, Cameroon, S4), 2 to 3 seeds per hill (Kenya, S9). Transplanting also used: transplant age about 7 days (2 true leaves) in the tropics (S2); 3 to 4 weeks after germination in greenhouse practice (S8); trays then transplanting at about 16 days after sowing in Mayotte trial (S3).

sowing_to_emergence_days.notes: Ngaoundere 2020: sown 28 Mar to 4 Apr, germination 8 Apr (rainy season); sown 15 to 18 Nov, germination 24 Nov (dry season) (S4). Range derived from those dates.

sowing_to_first_flower_days.notes: Flowering starts 40 to 45 days after sowing, within 30 days for early cultivars (S2). Ngaoundere: germination 8 Apr, first flower 5 May 2020, i.e. about 27 days after germination (S4).

observations.where: Southern Africa seed company guide, days after planting
Kenya farmer, Carmen F1, 'about 45 days to maturity'
Mayotte tunnel trial: transplanted 16 days after sowing, first harvest 29 to 32 days after transplanting (derived)
Philippines slicing types, days after planting

fruit_set_to_harvest_days.notes: Fruits picked 1 to 2 weeks after flowering (S2); pollination to harvest 15 to 18 days (S7).

observations.where: Mayotte tunnel trial, total harvest period
Up to 14 weeks with good pest and disease control (S7)
Early cultivars may die after 2 to 3 months in the field (crop life, not harvest window)
Kenya farmer: up to 8 harvests per crop before uprooting

total_cycle_days.notes: FAO-56 stage lengths for cucumber: 20/30/40/15 = 105 days and 25/35/50/20 = 130 days (arid regions) (S25). Mayotte trial last harvest at 96 days after transplanting, about 112 days after sowing (derived, S3). Lower bound 90 is an analyst rounding of first harvest (about 45) plus a short 45-day harvest; treat as indicative.

spacing_options.layout: Twin rows 100 x 50 x 50 cm (100 cm between pairs, 50 cm between twin rows, 50 cm in row)
75 cm between rows x 50 cm in row, 3 seeds per hill (Ngaoundere, Cameroon, 1,112 m)
90 x 100 cm, 2 to 3 seeds per hill (Kenya)
Hills 90 to 120 cm apart thinned to 2 to 3 plants, or rows 1 to 2 m apart with 30 cm in row
Rows 1.2 to 1.8 m, 50 cm to 1 m in row; or beds 1.2 to 1.8 m with 2 rows 40 cm apart, 50 to 80 cm in row
Furrows 0.75 to 1 m x 30 cm hills, 1 plant per hill after thinning (Philippines)
Beds 1.5 m between rows x 0.3 m in row, trellised single stem (tunnel, Mayotte)
40 x 20 cm (research plots, Ghana, best yield)
spacing_options.notes: Derived density; research plot, not a farm recommendation for trellised crops

recommended_density_plants_per_ha.notes: Analyst synthesis of the trellised slicing-cucumber layouts above (S1, S3, S8: 2.2 to 2.5 plants per m2). Max yield at 40,000 plants/ha was found in a 1992 Zaria trial (S23).

open_pollinated_kg_per_ha.notes: 1 to 3 kg/ha depending on sowing method (S2); 2 kg/ha (Philippines, S24).

derived_from_density_kg_per_ha.notes: Derived: 26,666 holes x 2 seeds (S1) x 1000-seed weight 20 to 35 g (S2).

hybrid_g_per_ha_farmer_example.notes: Derived from a Kenyan farmer using one 50 g sachet (KSh 450) of Carmen F1 on 0.5 acre (S10). Hybrids are sown more sparingly because of seed cost.

direct_seeded_slicing_temperate_kg_per_h.notes: Direct-seeded slicing cucumbers without precision seeder; about 2.25 kg/ha of seed gives enough transplants for 1 ha (British Columbia guide, temperate).

seeds_per_ha_derived.notes: Derived: 15,000 seeds per acre (Johnny's chart) / 0.4047 ha per acre = 37,065 seeds/ha.

trellising.practice: Staking strongly recommended for slicing cucumber: keeps fruit and leaves off the soil, reduces rot (S1). Wood or iron bars with ropes (Benin, S1). Single-stem training on horticultural string to a top wire (Mayotte, S3).
trellising.materials_described: Poles 2.5 m long, 2 to 2.5 inch diameter, 4 to 5 m apart along rows; No. 16 wire on top plus middle and lower wires; abaca or synthetic twine tied vertically at every hill (S24).

quantities_per_ha_derived.assumptions: Analyst derivation, not from a source: rows 1.0 to 1.5 m apart (6,667 to 10,000 m of row per ha), one post every 4 m (S7), 3 wire lines (S24), about 2 m of twine per plant at 22,000 to 26,666 plants/ha (S1, S3). End posts and anchors not included.

trellising.yield_effect: Uniben 2024 trial: no staking 2.29 t/ha, single staking 2.95 t/ha, trellis 2.74 t/ha, differences not significant (S20). Seed company says trellising gives better yields, no figure (S7).

mulch.practice: Layer of plant debris under developing fruits to avoid soil contact (Benin, S1). No plastic mulch rate found for cucumber in African sources.

itinerary.description: Slash vegetation manually or with a pre-plant non-selective herbicide. In Centre Cameroon, cucurbits (courge) are typically sown on slash-and-burn plots after fallow (S30). Burning is common but no quantified study of its effects on cucumber was found; agronomic risks (loss of organic matter, nutrient losses, bushfire, weed flush) are qualitative only. A Kenyan input supplier recommends Catapult 480SL at 250 ml per 20 L before planting (active ingredient not stated on the page).

inputs.product: Catapult 480SL (pre-plant herbicide, Kenya; active ingredient not stated in source)

itinerary.step: Tillage and bed or ridge making
itinerary.description: Till to about 30 cm then level (S1). Raised beds about 10 cm high and 60 cm wide used in the Mayotte trial (S3). Philippines guide uses ploughing, harrowing then furrowing or bedding (S24).
itinerary.labour_notes: Philippines: ploughing 6, harrowing 6, furrowing/bedding 4 man-days per ha (animal or tractor assisted context) (S24). No manual-tillage figure found for Cameroon.

itinerary.description: Well decomposed poultry manure or compost 20 t/ha placed in planting holes, 800 g per hole (S1). PROTA gives 25 to 35 t/ha organic manure (S2). Seed company guide: up to 20 t/ha manure plus 600 to 750 kg/ha Compound D basal (S7). Mayotte trial: 200 kg/ha NPK 15-12-24 at planting (S3). Philippines: 200 g manure per hill one week before planting plus about 15 g of 14-14-14 per hill (S24).

inputs.product: Poultry manure or compost, well decomposed
Compound D (basal compound, Southern Africa; formula not stated in source)

itinerary.labour_notes: Philippines: manure application 4 + basal fertilization 4 man-days (S24).

itinerary.description: Water holes well, sow 2 seeds per hole (S1) or 3 seeds per hill (S4), about 2 cm deep (S9). Kenyan establishment drench on input-supplier page: Pyramid 700WP 5 g/L + Loyalty 700WDG 10 g/20 L + Optimizer 1 ml/L (active ingredients not stated) (S9).

inputs.product: Cucumber seed, F1 hybrid (e.g. Tropicale F1, Kenzo F1, Sahira F1, Tokyo F1, Carmen F1, Nagano F1)

itinerary.description: Thin to one healthy plant per hill 2 to 3 weeks after planting (S24); PROTA hill system keeps 2 to 3 plants per hill (S2).

NPK 15-15-15 at 100 kg/ha (4 g per hole) 2 weeks after sowing (Benin, S1). Seed company guide: ammonium nitrate 50 kg/ha from 2 weeks after germination, repeated every 2 weeks until first fruit set (S7). PROTA: N every 2 to 3 weeks until fruit formation (S2). Nigerian trials: NPK 15-15-15 optimum about 120 kg/ha (S21); 30 to 60 kg N/ha tested at NIHORT (S16).

inputs.unit: kg/ha per application, every 2 weeks until first fruit set

itinerary.description: Install posts (1.6 to 1.8 m high, every 4 m) and wires before vines run; tie twine at each hill; train vines up (S7, S24). Pinch main-stem tip to encourage branching in non-trellised Kenyan practice (S9). Pinching at the 6th node with poultry manure gave the most marketable fruits in a Ghana trial (S22).
Second application of well decomposed organic matter, 400 g per hole at 4 weeks after sowing (Benin). Derived about 10.7 t/ha at 26,666 holes/ha.

At 6 weeks after sowing: mix of urea (25%) and potassium sulphate (75%) at 4 g per hole, derived about 107 kg/ha of mix (S1). Philippines: about 20 g per hill of urea and muriate of potash (2:1) about 1 month after sowing (S24). Seed company: muriate of potash 35 kg/ha after first fruit set, then with AN every 2 weeks (S7). Mayotte: 600 kg/ha NPK 15-12-24 split at 20 and 60 days after planting, with light earthing up (S3).

inputs.unit: kg/ha per application, repeated every 2 weeks with AN

itinerary.description: Kenyan input-supplier programme (trade names, compositions not stated): Goldchance Super Start 2.5 g/L or Lavender Super Start 1 ml/L at root development; Goldchance Super Growth 2.5 g/L or Lavender 1 ml/L at vegetative stage; Goldchance Super Flowers and Fruits 2.5 g/L, Vitabor Gold 1 ml/L (boron), Dimiphite 600 1.5 ml/L (P, K) at flowering and fruiting; Ferrari Gold 3 ml/L for calcium; sticker Integra 3 ml/20 L. No independent efficacy data found.

inputs.product: Starter foliar (Goldchance Super Start / Lavender Super Start)
Flowering/fruiting foliar (Goldchance Super Flowers and Fruits, Vitabor Gold, Dimiphite 600)

itinerary.description: Regular watering, especially at flowering and fruit set; drip, sprinkler or watering can; avoid overhead sprinklers from flowering on to prevent flower drop (S1). About 50 mm per week from flowering through fruit development, adjusted to pan evaporation (S7). Mayotte drip: 3 x 20 min per day with 1.1 L/h emitters every 30 cm, i.e. about 1.1 L per plant per day and about 2.4 mm/day (derived, tunnel, S3). FAO-56 crop coefficients: Kc ini 0.6, Kc mid 1.00, Kc end 0.75 (S25). Optimum rainfall about 800 mm, supplemented by irrigation (Kenya, S9).

irrigation_l_per_plant_per_day.notes: Derived from Mayotte drip set-up in a tunnel (S3); open-field needs in Foumbot dry season not measured.

itinerary.labour_notes: Philippines irrigation 4 man-days (furrow context) (S24); manual watering-can irrigation would need far more, no figure found.

itinerary.description: Hoeing every two weeks until flowering, then hand weeding until fruit maturity (Ngaoundere, Cameroon, S4). Three weeding/cultivation passes (Philippines, S24). Weed control also reduces Zeugodacus cucurbitae infestation (Cote d'Ivoire, S6).

Reference calendar from the CIRAD Mayotte trial (days after planting, 3-day pre-harvest interval): pymetrozine (Plenum 50 WG, 5 g/10 L) at 4, 43, 71 DAP for aphids and whiteflies; tau-fluvalinate (Klartan, 3 ml/10 L) at 36, 57, 78; deltamethrin + pirimicarb (Best, 20 ml/10 L) at 64; deltamethrin (Decis Protech, 10 ml/10 L) at 13, 29, 50, 85, 92 for caterpillars; preventive fungicide (Rocky + Dithane M-45, mancozeb) 3 weeks after sowing. Total 13 insecticide applications plus at least 1 fungicide (S3). Benin sheet: fruit flies controlled by burying rotten fruits outside the field, neem products and acetamiprid + lambda-cyhalothrin sprays (no dose); mites and leaf miners with neem or approved acaricide (S1). Kenyan supplier list gives trade-name products per pest (S9). In Cote d'Ivoire plots most recently treated with avermectin had lower fruit fly infestation (S6).

inputs.product: Neem-based products (fruit flies, mites, leaf miner); neem cake (nematodes)

sprays_per_cycle.notes: Only fully documented calendar is a tunnel trial in Mayotte (S3). Philippines cost table budgets 3 L/ha insecticide (S24).

itinerary.description: Cucumber is insect-pollinated. At Ngaoundere (Cameroon), bagged flowers set 0% fruit versus 72.5% (rainy season) and 78.3% (dry season) for open flowers; Apis mellifera made 63.53% of flower visits in the rainy season and accounted for 86.81% of fruit set (S4). Place 2 to 3 bee hives per ha; up to 8 bee visits per flower needed (S7). Avoid insecticide sprays during bee activity (bees active from 6 a.m., S4).

Harvest at 15 to 20 cm length and 4 to 7 cm diameter (S7), 20 to 25 cm for tropical types (S3), seeds still small and soft (S8). Frequency: 3 times per week (S8), 2 to 3 times per week (S26), every other day to every few days (S2), about every 5 days in Benin practice (S1), daily in the Mayotte trial (S3). Kenya farmer harvests at 6 to 8 inches, up to 8 harvests (S10).

inputs.product: Net bags (filets) as used at Mfoundi market, Yaounde (weight not stated)
Crates or cartons of 12 to 14 kg or 23 to 25 kg (international standard)

itinerary.labour_notes: Philippines harvesting budget 10 man-days (S24), which looks low for a multi-week harvest; no African figure found.

itinerary.description: Remove field heat quickly, grade and pack (S26). Store at 10 to 13 C and 90 to 95% RH, shelf life about 10 to 14 days (S7); 13 C and 95% RH for up to 14 days (S2). Chilling injury below 10 C, rapid yellowing above 16 C; tropical marketable life about 5 days without cooling (S2).

basis.notes: Derived: NPK gives 15-15-15; mix about 107 kg/ha = 26.7 kg urea (12.3 kg N) + 80 kg K2SO4 (about 40 kg K2O at standard 50% K2O).

basis.notes: Derived from 800 kg/ha total of 15-12-24; tunnel, drip, high yield.

basis.programme: Seed Co: Compound D 600 to 750 kg/ha basal, AN 50 kg/ha every 2 weeks to fruit set, KCl 35 kg/ha after fruit set, manure up to 20 t/ha
basis.notes: Compound D grade not stated in source.

basis.programme: Nigeria trials: optimum NPK 15-15-15 about 120 kg/ha (18 N, 18 P2O5, 18 K2O); Ghana best: 15 t/ha chicken manure + 50 kg/ha NPK; Zaria: highest yield at 75 kg N/ha

pests_diseases.name: Fruit flies (Dacus bivittatus, Dacus ciliatus major in Cameroon; also Zeugodacus/Bactrocera cucurbitae, D. vertebratus, D. punctatifrons)
pests_diseases.importance: Major. Cucurbit fruit losses to tephritids about 36.7% at Yaounde and 37.1% at Koutaba (Noun division, next to Foumbot) in 2009 to 2011; losses on cucumber higher at Koutaba (S5). Cote d'Ivoire 2023: 90% of cucurbit plots infested, mean 30.5% of fruits damaged; less than half of cucumbers yielded no pupae; Z. cucurbitae higher in rainy season May to July (S6).
pests_diseases.controls: Sanitation (collect and bury infested fruits), weed control, neem, acetamiprid + lambda-cyhalothrin (S1); avermectin associated with lower infestation (S6); insect-proof netting (S6).

pests_diseases.name: Aphids
pests_diseases.controls: Pymetrozine 5 g/10 L; deltamethrin + pirimicarb (S3). Kenyan trade product Pentagon 50EC 0.5 ml/L (S9).

pests_diseases.name: Whiteflies
pests_diseases.importance: Listed pest and virus vector (S2, S7).
pests_diseases.controls: Pymetrozine (S3); Profile 440EC 1.5 ml/L (Kenya, a.i. not stated) (S9).

pests_diseases.name: Melon worm / pickleworm (Diaphania hyalinata) and other caterpillars (armyworms, cutworms)
pests_diseases.importance: Listed pest (S2); caterpillar sprays 5 times in Mayotte (S3).
pests_diseases.controls: Deltamethrin 10 ml/10 L (S3); cutworm soil drench Profile 440EC 3 ml/L (S9).

pests_diseases.name: Red spider mites (Tetranychus spp.)
pests_diseases.controls: Neem products or acaricide (S1); Alonze 50EC 3 ml/20 L (Kenya) (S9).

pests_diseases.name: Root-knot nematodes (Meloidogyne spp.)
pests_diseases.controls: Solarization, flooding, sanitary fallow, rotation, heavy organic matter, neem cake (S1).

pests_diseases.name: Downy mildew (Pseudoperonospora cubensis)
pests_diseases.importance: Main foliar disease in humid conditions; observed in Mayotte trial; smooth (European) varieties much more sensitive than tropical types (S2, S3).
pests_diseases.controls: Preventive mancozeb (S3); Kenyan trade products Gearlock Turbo 250WP 25 g/20 L (S9).

pests_diseases.name: Other fungal and bacterial diseases: target leaf spot, gummy stem blight, angular leaf spot, Fusarium wilt, damping off, scab, Phytophthora fruit rot, belly rot, Alternaria, Choanephora
pests_diseases.importance: Listed for tropical Africa incl. Cote d'Ivoire (S2).
pests_diseases.controls: Seed and soil hygiene; Kenyan drench products for damping off and Fusarium (S9).

pests_diseases.name: Viruses (CMV, ZYMV, PRSV, CVYV, CGMMV)
pests_diseases.importance: Listed (S2); unidentified viruses observed in Mayotte (S3).

labour_notes: No Cameroonian or itemised African figure found. Philippines DA cost table lists about 86 man-days/ha (sum of items, trellising 40, harvest 10, excluding spraying) (S24). Kaduna (Nigeria) survey reports only 15 to 17 man-days/ha, which looks understated (S17). NIHORT Ibadan: labour is 60% of total production cost (S16). Treat as low confidence; fully manual production with watering cans in Foumbot will likely exceed 86.

post_harvest_notes: No measured post-harvest loss percentage found for cucumber in Cameroon or the region. Shelf life about 5 days without cooling in the tropics, yellowing above 16 C, chilling injury below 10 C (S2). Separate field (pre-harvest) losses from fruit flies: about 36.7 to 37.1% of cucurbit fruits in Cameroon (S5) and 30.5% in Cote d'Ivoire (S6).

prices.unit_notes: Cameroon wholesale cucumbers move in net bags (filets) of unstated weight; retail in heaps (tas) or per piece (S11). Foreign prices kept in local currency because no sourced exchange rate was collected. XOF (Cote d'Ivoire) and XAF (Cameroon) are at par, both pegged at 655.957 per euro, so Ivorian FCFA prices are entered directly as XAF (analyst note, no conversion).

prices.seasonality: Yaounde: vegetables abundant and cheap in the rainy season, dearer in the dry season because fields must be irrigated (S11, Aug 2021). Kenya: price rises from KSh 20 to 50/kg in high demand periods (S10). Philippines: off-season price 67% above regular season (S24). No month-by-month cucumber price series for Foumbot, Bafoussam or Yaounde was found; INS price notes report only a vegetable index (no cucumber line). Abidjan CNLVC series (S31 to S37): 350 FCFA/kg in Mar, Oct and Dec 2024; 400 mid-Mar 2024; 500 in Feb-Mar 2025; 600 in Aug and Nov 2025, so a rising trend that mixes seasonality and inflation. Sika Finance Sep 2026: 350 (Bouake) to 600 FCFA/kg (Abidjan, Yamoussoukro) (S38). Kinshasa crate up 42% between May and June 2024, attributed partly to seasonality (S39).

optimal_day_temp_c.notes: About 30 C optimum (S2); 25 to 30 C (S8); 20 to 25 C (S7); 25 C (S1); 18 to 30 C range (S9).

minimum_temp_c.notes: 15 C minimum for good development (S2); growth slows below 16 C (S7); soil at least 13 C for direct seeding (S7).

climate.heat_notes: No explicit field heat-stress threshold found in sources. Post-harvest yellowing above 16 C (S2) is a storage threshold, not a field one.

altitude_m.notes: Up to 2000 m in tropical Africa (S2); up to 1700 m (Kenya, S9). Foumbot (1,000 to 1,200 m) is inside the range; a MINADER station trial at 1,112 m in Ngaoundere succeeded in both seasons (S4).

rainfall_mm.notes: Optimum about 800 mm, supplemented with irrigation (S9).

climate.rain_humidity_sensitivity: Humid conditions favour downy mildew, powdery mildew, anthracnose, Alternaria, Cladosporium; smooth European varieties much more sensitive than tropical types (S3). Overhead watering at flowering causes flower drop (S1). Fruit fly Z. cucurbitae and weed cover higher in the rainy season (May to July) in Cote d'Ivoire (S6).

planting_windows_foumbot.proposal: Window A: sow at onset of rains, mid-March to April, rainfed, harvest May to July. Window B: sow late rains, September to October, finish in early dry season (lower disease pressure, possibly better prices). Window C: dry season November to February only with irrigation.
planting_windows_foumbot.basis: Analyst inference, not a sourced recommendation for Foumbot. Supported by Ngaoundere (1,112 m, one rainy season) trials sown 28 Mar to 4 Apr and 15 to 18 Nov, both setting fruit well with bees (S4); dry-season price premium in Yaounde (S11); rainy-season pest peaks (S6).

confidence_notes: OVERALL: medium for agronomy, low for Cameroon economics. (1) Naming: Cameroon 'concombre' statistics (FAOSTAT 262,000 to 265,000 t; AGRISTAT 282,773 t) are 45 times Temple's 1998 figure of 5,877 t and dwarf Kenya (14,404 t) and Ghana (135 t); they very probably include Cucumeropsis mannii seed cucumber. Do not use them to size the fresh cucumber market without verification with MINADER/AGRISTAT. (2) No Cameroon or Foumbot farm-level cost of production, labour, or yield survey for Cucumis sativus was found. The only Cameroon field trial (Ngaoundere 2020-21, S4) reports pollination and fruit traits, not t/ha. (3) Cameroon prices: one wholesale observation (2,000 FCFA per filet of unknown weight, Yaounde, Aug 2021) and one 1998 national average (359 FCFA/kg). The filet weight is a critical gap; field measurement in Foumbot/Bafoussam markets is needed. (4) Labour figures come from the Philippines (86 man-days) and a weak Nigerian paper (15 to 17); itemised African labour data is a gap. (5) Spray calendar is from a tunnel trial in Mayotte; open-field rainy-season Foumbot conditions probably need more fungicide. (6) Several derived numbers (seed kg/ha, trellis quantities, nutrient totals, l/plant/day, price per kg from per-piece price) are marked 'derived' with their assumptions. (7) Blocked or unavailable during research: FAOSTAT API (area and yield for Cameroon), Infonet-Biovision, Martinique Chamber of Agriculture technical sheets, full text of Mokam et al. 2018; web search quota ran out before Ghana MoFA, KALRO/HCD, Technisem/Tropicasem and ANADER guides could be located. Varieties Darina F1 and others named in the brief were not found in sources and are not included. FOLLOW-UP ROUND (Oct 2026): added a Cote d'Ivoire per-kg price series (2024 to 2026, CNLVC via Fraternite Matin and Sika Finance), Kenya farmgate (FAOSTAT via Selina, Jan 2024) and HCDA 2011-13 implied prices and yields, Kinshasa crate and Cape Coast basket prices (unit weights unknown), fruit weights of varieties sold in Central Africa, Kenyan seed pack prices and temperate seed-quantity references. Still missing: any Cameroon farm-gate or wholesale price per kg after 2021, the filet weight, Cameroon seed prices, post-harvest loss %, and Cameroon cost of production. Ivorian prices are probably consumer-level and should be treated as an upper bound for farm-gate prices. Selina Wamucii and Tridge figures have undisclosed or inconsistent methodology.
